name: Trazodone
drug_class: Serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitor (SARI); triazolopyridine
route_note: Oral tablets, usually in divided doses or at bedtime; extended-release forms in some countries.

discovery.by: Angelini Research Laboratories (Bruno Silvestrini and colleagues)
discovery.note: Developed in Italy in the 1960s from a hypothesis linking depression to altered pain thresholds.

tagline: Sedating antidepressant widely used at low doses for insomnia
summary: Trazodone is a triazolopyridine antidepressant that blocks 5-HT2A receptors and weakly inhibits serotonin reuptake. Developed in Italy in the 1960s, it is licensed for depression but is very widely used off-label at low doses as a hypnotic.
mechanism: At low doses trazodone acts mainly as an antagonist at 5-HT2A, histamine H1 and alpha-1 adrenergic receptors, producing sedation. At higher antidepressant doses, serotonin transporter inhibition adds a serotonergic effect while 5-HT2A blockade limits insomnia, anxiety and sexual side effects.
Its metabolite m-chlorophenylpiperazine (mCPP) is a serotonin receptor agonist. Alpha-1 blockade underlies orthostatic hypotension and the rare risk of priapism.

history.title: Italian launch
history.detail: Trazodone is marketed in Italy as Trittico.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Desyrel (Mead Johnson) for depression.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic trazodone becomes available in the US.

history.title: Suicidality warning
history.detail: Class boxed warning on suicidality in young people.

history.title: Oleptro
history.detail: A once-daily extended-release form is approved in the US.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP3A4 to active mCPP (further via CYP2D6)

safety.boxed_warning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours in children, adolescents and young adults (under 25) taking antidepressants; monitor for clinical worsening.

facts: Trazodone is among the most prescribed sleep aids in the US despite lacking an insomnia indication.
